conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is not supported by scientific evidence, citing major health organizations (NCI, ACS, National Academies, Komen) that agree there is no causal link between abortion and breast cancer. Thus, it clearly rejects the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
The claim that abortion increases breast cancer risk is not supported by mainstream scientific evidence. This is a long-settled question that continues to be promoted mainly by advocacy groups rather than the medical/scientific establishment.

In 2003, the National Cancer Institute convened over 100 leading experts to review population, clinical, and animal studies. They concluded there is no causal relationship between induced abortion and breast cancer risk (https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk). The American Cancer Society reaffirms this, noting that a 2018 report from the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine also concluded abortion does not affect breast cancer risk, and that "higher-quality studies have generally found no link" (https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html). Susan G. Komen, a major breast cancer research and advocacy organization, states plainly that research "clearly shows" no increased risk, citing agreement from ACOG and NCI (https://www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/).

The contrary claim is promoted largely by anti-abortion advocacy sites (e.g., Illinois Family Institute, Life Research Institute, abortionbreastcancer.com) and cites older or lower-quality studies, often plagued by recall bias—women with cancer are more likely to disclose past abortions than healthy controls, artificially inflating apparent associations. Wikipedia notes this hypothesis "is at odds with mainstream scientific opinion and is rejected by major medical professional organizations," despite continuing to be propagated as pseudoscience (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion–breast_cancer_hypothesis).

**Conclusion:** The claim is not supported by the weight of scientific evidence. Major health and cancer research bodies (NCI, ACS, National Academies, Komen) agree there is no causal link, while contrary claims rely on methodologically weaker studies and advocacy interpretation.
